title: Everything on ImpactMojo about gender, in one place
description: A roundup of every gender-related resource on the platform: three flagship courses, six 101 decks, three Studios, three Fundamentals pages, two deep dives, six reading companions, a timeline, a game, a challenge and the printable handouts — with what each is for, and the three gaps still open.

title: Animal Welfare Law and the Fifty-Rupee Fine
description: India's Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act sets a maximum first-offence fine of fifty rupees, unchanged since 1960 and worth ₹3.79 today. Plus what Animal Ask's 2026 prioritisation of Indian animal advocacy says about enforcement as the highest-leverage reform, and why framing decides whether an ask travels.
tags: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act

title: The Social Model of Disability
description: The social model of disability, made clickable. Six Indian outcomes drawn as barrier stacks across attitudinal, environmental, institutional and communication barriers — entering a public building, boarding a bus, finishing school, getting a job, being counted, and holding the disability certificate — each with the NSS 76th Round figure, the RPwD Act provision or the judgment behind it, and what the model leaves unsettled in an Indian context.

title: The Sustainable Livelihoods Framework
description: DFID's Sustainable Livelihoods Framework, made clickable. Eight Indian livelihoods drawn as asset pentagons across human, social, natural, physical and financial capital — a marginal farmer, a landless labourer, a large landholder, a forest-dwelling household, a pastoralist, a marine fisher, a seasonal migrant and a home-based worker — shown together so the shapes can be compared, each with its vulnerability context and the survey or statute behind every corner.

title: Practical and Strategic Gender Needs
description: Caroline Moser's distinction between practical gender needs and strategic gender interests, made clickable. Twelve Indian interventions plotted by how much material burden each lifts off a woman's day and how far it moves the division of labour, assets or authority — from Ujjwala and Jal Jeevan to the 73rd Amendment and the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act — each with the survey, statute or judgment behind its position.

title: The Capability Approach
description: Sen's capability approach made clickable: five resources followed from what a programme provides to what a person can actually do with it, with the Indian evidence at each step — school places against reading levels, toilets built against toilets used, income against life expectancy. Includes Nussbaum's ten central capabilities.

title: The Science and Application of Positive Psychology
description: Interactive companion to Cheavens and Feldman's textbook: the negativity asymmetry that justifies studying the positive, hope and goal theory, character strengths, and a research-literacy chapter for telling positive psychology apart from the pop psychology that borrows its vocabulary.

title: Unlimited Memory
description: Interactive companion to Kevin Horsley's memory-technique manual: the SEE principle, the journey and peg methods, number and name systems, and spaced review — with a note on where a popular technique book sits next to the cognitive science.

title: Public Health, Ethics, and Equity
description: Interactive companion to Anand, Peter and Sen's volume on health equity: the social gradient, Rawlsian arguments about when a health inequality is unjust, the ethics of DALYs and cost-effectiveness analysis, and Sen's external vs internal perspectives on illness.

title: The p-value answers a question you probably aren't asking
description: A p-value and a confidence interval answer different questions. Knowing which is which changes what you do with a result, with a worked example from a programme evaluation.

title: Farm Animal Welfare in India
description: A curated reading list on Indian farm animal welfare: the Livestock Census numbers, the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, the 2014 Supreme Court judgment on animal dignity, the unnotified 2017 cage-free rules, and the peer-reviewed evidence on dairy cattle.

Understand paid and unpaid care work, why GDP hides it, how India's Time Use Survey measures it, the 5 Rs framework, care policies and the case for investing in care. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: SEL Basics 101
description: SEL Basics 101 — a free foundational course for educators and education-programme staff in South Asia. Understand social and emotional learning: the CASEL five competencies, the evidence base, classroom practice, measurement cautions and how to contextualise SEL for India and the region. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Sexual Health 101
description: Sexual Health 101 — a free, rights-based foundational course on sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) for development and health practitioners in South Asia: from the WHO definition and the ICPD framework to contraception, maternal health, safe abortion, STIs and HIV, comprehensive sexuality education, consent and youth-friendly services. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Community Development 101
description: Community Development 101 — a free foundational course for development practitioners in South Asia. Participation, empowerment, asset-based approaches, community organising, participatory tools, self-help groups, power and elite capture, sustainability and panchayati raj — from Arnstein and Chambers to Ostrom and India's DAY-NRLM. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Education and Pedagogy 101
description: Education and Pedagogy 101 — a free foundational course for educators and education-programme staff in South Asia. From how learning works and Bloom's taxonomy to constructivist and inclusive practice, assessment, foundational literacy and numeracy, Teaching at the Right Level, Freire's critical pedagogy and India's learning crisis. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: English for Development 101
description: English for Development 101 — a free, practical communication course for NGO staff, researchers and grant writers across South Asia working in English as a second or third language: plain writing, killing jargon, structuring reports, communicating data and speaking with confidence. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Decolonial Development 101
description: Decolonial Development 101 — a free foundational course for practitioners, researchers and students in the Global South and South Asia. From the colonial roots of 'development' and the coloniality of power to epistemic injustice, decolonising aid and research, and post-development alternatives like buen vivir, ubuntu and swaraj. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Digital Ethics 101
description: Digital Ethics 101 — a free foundational course for development practitioners in South Asia on deploying digital technology responsibly: data privacy and the DPDP Act, algorithmic bias, AI, digital identity, surveillance, the digital divide, platform power, online harms and responsible design. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Environmental Justice 101
description: Environmental Justice 101 — a free foundational course for development and environment practitioners in South Asia. Who bears environmental harm and who reaps its benefits: from caste, class and Adivasi rights to climate justice, the Forest Rights Act, pollution and just transition. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Post-Truth Politics 101
description: Post-Truth Politics 101 — a free foundational course for development practitioners, communicators and citizens in South Asia on why emotion, identity and falsehood beat facts: from mis- and disinformation to echo chambers, the believing brain, the attention economy, synthetic media and building resilience through media literacy. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Visual Ethnography 101
description: Visual Ethnography 101 — a free foundational course for development researchers and communicators in South Asia. Read, make and analyse images responsibly: photo-elicitation, photovoice, video methods, the ethics of the gaze, and dignified representation in field work. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Indian Constitution 101
description: Indian Constitution 101 — a free foundational course on the making, structure and living practice of the Constitution of India, for development practitioners, students and citizens. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Global Development Governance 101
description: Global Development Governance 101 — a free foundational course for development practitioners in South Asia. Understand the global aid architecture: the UN system, the World Bank and IMF, ODA and the OECD-DAC, the SDGs, financing for development, new actors, aid effectiveness, the critiques of aid, and India's shift from recipient to donor. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Public Health 101
description: Public Health 101 — a free foundational course for development and health practitioners in South Asia: population health and prevention, social determinants, epidemiology, disease burden, health systems and India's path to universal health coverage. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Fundraising Basics 101
description: Fundraising Basics 101 — a free foundational course for NGO and nonprofit staff in India and South Asia. From mission-first resource mobilisation and the funding landscape to proposals, budgets, CSR under the Companies Act, FCRA and 80G compliance, donor relationships and the ethics of fundraising. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Theory of Change 101
description: Theory of Change 101 — a free, practical course for development practitioners in programme design and M&E across South Asia: build a causal map from activities to long-term change, surface assumptions, choose indicators, draw the outcome pathway, dodge the common pitfalls and use a ToC across the whole programme cycle. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Advocacy Basics 101
description: Advocacy Basics 101 — a free foundational course for development and civil-society practitioners in South Asia: how to analyse power, frame an issue, map stakeholders, build a strategy and theory of change, read policy windows, choose tactics, and advocate ethically. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Behaviour Change Communication 101
description: Behaviour Change Communication 101 — a free foundational course for development and public-health communicators in South Asia. From the awareness-action gap to behaviour theories, audience research, message design, channels, campaigns and ethics — with India-centric examples. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Political Economy 101
description: Political Economy 101 — a free foundational course for development practitioners and analysts in South Asia. From Smith, Ricardo and Marx through institutions, collective action, rents and political settlements to Political Economy Analysis in practice and the Indian state. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Women's Economic Empowerment 101
description: Women's Economic Empowerment 101 — a free foundational course for gender and development practitioners in South Asia: resources, agency and achievements; the unpaid care economy; women's labour force participation; pay gaps; land, finance and enterprise; norms, rights and what works. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Child Development 101
description: Child Development 101 — a free foundational course on early childhood development for health and development practitioners in South Asia: the first 1,000 days, domains and theories of development, nutrition, health, responsive caregiving, the Nurturing Care Framework, adversity, India's ECD ecosystem and how to measure it. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Feminist Research 101
description: Feminist Research 101 — a free foundational course for development researchers and practitioners in South Asia. From the feminist critique of objective science through standpoint theory, situated knowledges and intersectionality to ethics, reflexivity, decolonial feminisms and a practical checklist for doing research that challenges power. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Gender Mainstreaming 101
description: Gender Mainstreaming 101 — a free foundational course for development practitioners and programme managers in South Asia: from the Beijing Platform and ECOSOC definition to gender analysis, the programme cycle, gender-responsive budgeting, the twin-track approach, institutionalisation and the critiques that keep it honest. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Impact Evaluation 101
description: Impact Evaluation 101 — a free foundational course for development programme and MEL practitioners in South Asia on designing, commissioning and using credible impact evaluations: the counterfactual, theory of change, RCTs, quasi-experimental designs, power, measurement, interpretation, cost and ethics, with India-centric examples. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Maternal Health 101
description: Maternal Health 101 — a free foundational course for development and public-health practitioners in South Asia: why mothers die, the three delays, the continuum of care, antenatal and emergency obstetric care, family planning and safe abortion, equity, and India's programmes from JSY to SUMAN. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Mixed Methods 101
description: Mixed Methods 101 — a free foundational course for development researchers and MEL practitioners in South Asia on intentionally combining quantitative and qualitative evidence within a single study: the core designs, integration, quality and worked examples. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: Survey Design 101
description: Survey Design 101 — a free foundational course for development and MEL practitioners running field surveys in South Asia. From objectives and questionnaire design to sampling, modes, translation, pretesting, fieldwork quality and survey ethics under the DPDP Act. ImpactMojo, CC BY-NC-ND.

title: The Long View — An ImpactMojo Original Data-Visualization Studio
description: ImpactMojo's own data-visualization studio and a gallery of the greats. Original charts built by hand from real, cited evidence on poverty, child survival, caste, climate and women's work; flow forms including Sankey, alluvial and a hub Sankey of the Union Budget; four map forms of the same country (hex cartogram, dot-density map, Dorling cartogram and a tilegram of 121 hexagons); original diagrams of the frameworks we teach (Arnstein's ladder, the results chain, the poverty trap, intersectionality, the systems iceberg); hand-coded recreations of the timeless classics (Nightingale, Minard, Snow, Du Bois); and a curated gallery of modern masterworks from Gapminder, Our World in Data, The Pudding, ProPublica, PARI and more.

title: Numbers in the News — a reader's field guide

Scrapers are Apache-2.0, the compiled data CC BY 4.0. No district or trial court decisions.

An independent project by Nand Lal Mishra and Swati Sneha, not an official IIPS or MoHFW release.

title: Development Law Docket
description: Indian judgments that changed what development organisations, programmes and rights-holders can do — what each decided, what it changed, and whether it still stands.

title: Aureliano Fernandes v. State of Goa
description: Found serious gaps in POSH implementation across public and private institutions and directed verification that Internal Committees actually exist and function.

title: Deepika Singh v. Central Administrative Tribunal
description: Atypical families — including single-parent, queer and reconstituted households — are entitled to equal protection of benefits like maternity leave.

title: Noel Harper v. Union of India
description: Upheld the 2020 FCRA amendments, including the bar on transferring foreign contribution to other organisations and mandatory SBI New Delhi account opening.

title: X v. Principal Secretary, Health & Family Welfare, NCT of Delhi
description: Unmarried women are entitled to termination up to 24 weeks on the same terms as married women; 'husband' in the MTP Rules is read as 'partner'.

title: State of Kerala v. Leesamma Joseph
description: Reservation for persons with disabilities applies to promotion, not only to entry-level recruitment.

title: Vikash Kumar v. Union Public Service Commission
description: Reasonable accommodation is a substantive right, not a concession; denying a scribe to a candidate with writer's cramp because he fell outside the benchmark-disability category was discriminatory.

title: Alembic Pharmaceuticals v. Rohit Prajapati
description: Ex post facto environmental clearance is contrary to law; a project cannot regularise construction already carried out without clearance.

title: Secretary, Ministry of Defence v. Babita Puniya
description: Directed grant of permanent commission to women officers in the Army, rejecting arguments from physiological differences and troop attitudes.

title: Indian Social Action Forum (INSAF) v. Union of India
description: Read down the 'organisation of a political nature' provisions so that ordinary advocacy and rights work does not, by itself, disqualify an organisation from foreign funding.

title: In Re: Problems and Miseries of Migrant Labourers
description: In suo motu proceedings during the COVID-19 lockdown, directed transport, dry rations and registration for stranded migrant workers.

title: Hanuman Laxman Aroskar v. Union of India
description: Suspended an airport's environmental clearance for non-disclosure and inadequate appraisal, holding that the EIA process must be substantively, not formally, complied with.

title: CPIO, Supreme Court of India v. Subhash Chandra Agarwal
description: The office of the Chief Justice of India is a public authority under the RTI Act; judicial independence is not a blanket exemption from disclosure.

title: Common Cause v. Union of India
description: Recognised the right to die with dignity, permitting passive euthanasia and advance directives with procedural safeguards.

title: Joseph Shine v. Union of India
description: Struck down adultery as a criminal offence, holding it treated a wife as her husband's property.

title: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
description: Section 377 IPC is unconstitutional insofar as it criminalises consensual sexual acts between adults.

title: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (Aadhaar)
description: Upheld Aadhaar for subsidies and welfare under Section 7, struck down mandatory linking by private entities and Section 57.

title: Disabled Rights Group v. Union of India
description: Directed enforcement of the statutory reservation for persons with disabilities in higher education institutions, including centrally funded ones.

title: Independent Thought v. Union of India
description: Read down the exception permitting marital intercourse with a wife aged 15 to 18, making it rape.

title: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (Privacy)
description: A nine-judge bench held privacy is a fundamental right intrinsic to Article 21, and set a proportionality test for any intrusion.

title: Rajive Raturi v. Union of India
description: Directed Union and State governments to make public buildings, transport and information accessible within fixed timelines under the RPwD Act.

title: Shayara Bano v. Union of India
description: Set aside instant triple talaq as arbitrary and not protected as an essential religious practice.

title: Jeeja Ghosh v. Union of India
description: Offloading a passenger with cerebral palsy without assessment violated her dignity; the Court awarded compensation and stressed the social model of disability.

title: Swaraj Abhiyan v. Union of India
description: Directed States to declare drought where conditions warranted and to implement NFSA and MGNREGA entitlements during it.

title: Laxmi v. Union of India
description: Directed regulation of acid sales, compensation for survivors, and treatment obligations on hospitals.

title: Reserve Bank of India v. Jayantilal N. Mistry
description: A regulator cannot claim a fiduciary relationship with the entities it regulates to withhold inspection reports from the public.

title: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
description: Struck down Section 66A of the IT Act as vague and overbroad, and read down intermediary takedown obligations.

title: Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh
description: Registration of an FIR is mandatory where information discloses a cognizable offence; a preliminary inquiry is permitted only in limited categories.

title: Orissa Mining Corporation v. Ministry of Environment & Forests (Niyamgiri)
description: Referred the question of religious and cultural rights over the Niyamgiri hills to the Gram Sabhas, whose decision would bind the clearance process.

title: Girish Ramchandra Deshpande v. Central Information Commissioner
description: Service records, assets and disciplinary details of a public servant are 'personal information' exempt under Section 8(1)(j) unless a larger public interest is shown.

title: Medha Kotwal Lele v. Union of India
description: Found the Vishaka guidelines widely unimplemented and issued directions to States and regulators to bring complaints mechanisms into being.

title: Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India
description: Directed action against trafficking of children into circuses and for their rescue and rehabilitation.

title: Nandini Sundar v. State of Chhattisgarh
description: Held the arming of civilians as Special Police Officers in counter-insurgency unconstitutional and directed disbanding of Salwa Judum.

title: Suchita Srivastava v. Chandigarh Administration
description: Reproductive choice is personal liberty under Article 21; pregnancy could not be terminated against the will of a woman with intellectual disability.

title: Anuj Garg v. Hotel Association of India
description: Struck down a prohibition on women working in premises serving liquor as protective discrimination that failed strict scrutiny.

title: Prakash Singh v. Union of India
description: Issued seven binding directions on police reform, including fixed tenure, a State Security Commission, and separation of investigation from law and order.

title: T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka
description: An eleven-judge bench held that private unaided institutions have autonomy in administration and admissions, subject to regulation against maladministration.

title: Apparel Export Promotion Council v. A.K. Chopra
description: Sexual harassment does not require physical contact; conduct that outrages a woman's modesty and creates a hostile environment is enough to justify dismissal.

title: Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh
description: Transfer of land in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals, including government leases to private mining companies, is void under the Fifth Schedule regime.

title: Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan
description: Absent a law on workplace sexual harassment, the Court framed binding guidelines under Article 32 and declared them enforceable until Parliament legislated.

title: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal
description: Laid down mandatory safeguards for arrest and detention — memo of arrest, informing a relative, medical examination, and a record.

title: T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad v. Union of India
description: Gave 'forest' its dictionary meaning regardless of ownership or classification, and placed forest governance under continuing court supervision.

title: M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu
description: Directed elimination of child labour in hazardous industries with employer contributions to a welfare fund and compulsory education for the withdrawn child.

title: Paschim Banga Khet Mazdoor Samity v. State of West Bengal
description: Denial of emergency medical treatment by a government hospital violates Article 21; the State must provide adequate emergency facilities.

title: Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v. Union of India
description: Adopted the precautionary principle and the polluter-pays principle as part of Indian environmental law.

title: Chameli Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh
description: The right to shelter is part of the right to life, extending beyond a roof to civic amenities that make a dwelling liveable.

title: Unni Krishnan, J.P. v. State of Andhra Pradesh
description: Recognised a fundamental right to free education up to age 14, and framed a scheme regulating private professional institutions.

title: Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka
description: Charging capitation fees was unconstitutional; the right to education flows from the right to life.

title: Subhash Kumar v. State of Bihar
description: The right to life includes the right to enjoy pollution-free water and air.

title: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum Gas Leak)
description: Established absolute liability: an enterprise in a hazardous activity is liable for harm without exceptions, and the measure of damages scales with its capacity to pay.

title: Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation
description: The right to life under Article 21 includes the right to livelihood; pavement dwellers could not be evicted without due process, though eviction itself was permitted.

title: Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India
description: Treated a letter as a writ petition, relaxed standing, and held that bonded labour is a violation of Article 21 requiring identification, release and rehabilitation.

title: Francis Coralie Mullin v. Administrator, Union Territory of Delhi
description: Article 21 means more than animal existence: it includes living with human dignity and the bare necessities of life.

title: Municipal Council, Ratlam v. Vardhichand
description: A municipality cannot plead lack of funds to escape its statutory duty to provide sanitation and abate a public nuisance.

title: Hussainara Khatoon v. Home Secretary, State of Bihar
description: Undertrials detained longer than the maximum sentence must be released; speedy trial and free legal aid are part of Article 21.

title: Sampurna Behura v. Union of India
description: Found the Juvenile Justice Act substantially unimplemented and directed States to fill vacancies and constitute the bodies the Act requires.

title: Devika Biswas v. Union of India
description: Condemned mass sterilisation camps as a violation of reproductive autonomy and Article 21, and directed States to close camp-based targets.

title: National Legal Services Authority v. Union of India
description: Recognised transgender persons as a third gender with the right to self-identify, and directed reservation and welfare measures.

title: Society for Un-aided Private Schools of Rajasthan v. Union of India
description: Upheld the RTE Act's requirement that private unaided schools reserve 25% of Class I places for children from weaker and disadvantaged groups.

title: Consumer Education & Research Centre v. Union of India
description: The right to health and to a safe working environment is part of Article 21; asbestos workers were entitled to medical monitoring and compensation.

title: People's Union for Civil Liberties v. Union of India (ICDS / Anganwadi directions)
description: In the right-to-food litigation, directed that every sanctioned Anganwadi Centre be made operational and that ICDS reach children, adolescent girls, and pregnant and lactating women.

title: People's Union for Civil Liberties v. Union of India (mid-day meal directions)
description: Restates and enforces the Court's direction of 28 November 2001 that every child in every government and government-assisted primary school receive a cooked mid-day meal of at least 300 calories and 8–12 grams of protein, for a minimum of 200 school days, and requires States still giving dry rations to move to cooked meals on a fixed timetable.

title: Union Budget Explorer — where the Union rupee goes
description: What the Government of India collects and what it spends it on, head by head, with eight years of actual spending from 2017-18 to 2024-25 beside the current budget — and what your own income tax works out to across defence, interest, education, health and rural development. Source: Budget at a Glance, Ministry of Finance.

title: Dividing Good by Money: Effective Altruism, Cost per Outcome, and What Arithmetic Cannot Settle
description: The strongest case for letting cost-effectiveness decide, the five objections that defeat it — aggregation, structural injustice, the measurement gradient, who defines the outcome, and expected value without a portfolio — and eight working principles that keep the counting while withdrawing its authority to conclude. Fully sourced.

title: The judgment you cited may have been overruled
description: A Supreme Court judgment was delivered in May 2025, recalled on review in November, and reheard in July 2026, and nothing in anyone's files changed on any of those dates. Why development documents carry stale case law, what to check before citing a judgment, and what became free to check this year — Supreme Court open data, India Open Law's 12.8 million judgments and 813,168 tribunal matters, and eCourts.

title: What India's unemployment rate hides about who works
description: By social group the unemployment rate moves 1.6 points while labour-force participation moves twenty, in the other direction, so reading the rate alone inverts the picture. Why the two rates have different denominators, and the rule thirteen ImpactMojo data explorers ended up following: never show a headline number without the number that changes its meaning, and say what the page cannot tell you.

title: NFHS State Explorer — rural and urban India, side by side
description: India's health and nutrition indicators by state, with rural and urban shown separately rather than combined into one figure. 136 indicators across NFHS-4 (2015-16) and NFHS-5 (2019-21) — stunting, anaemia, institutional births, immunisation, sanitation, women's empowerment and more — ranked by the size of the rural-urban gap, with what changed between the rounds for each half separately. Source: MoSPI eSankhyiki NFHS data service.

title: ResGov Budget Insights & Research
description: Ministry-by-ministry Union Budget analysis from the Foundation for Responsive Governance — 50 Budget Insights briefs plus working papers and reports on welfare delivery and state capacity. PDFs rather than a dataset.

title: CSR Explorer — where India's corporate social responsibility money goes
description: Five years of India's mandated CSR spending, 2018-19 to 2022-23, from Ministry of Corporate Affairs data. Which states received it, which development sectors absorbed it, and how much was assigned to no state at all. CSR per resident tracks state income far more closely than state need: Delhi received about ₹884 per person in 2022-23 against Bihar's ₹23, and education and health together took more than half of all spending. Source: Ministry of Corporate Affairs via data.gov.in, with Census 2011 population and per-capita NSDP.

title: Prisons & Undertrials Explorer — who is actually in prison in India?
description: 73.5% of India's 530,333 prisoners are undertrials: people in custody whose trial has not concluded, who in law are innocent. Prison Statistics India 2023 and court pendency, by state — occupancy against sanctioned capacity, how long undertrials have already waited, the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe share of undertrials against their share of the population, schooling reached, Section 436A releases, and the 44.9 million cases pending in district courts. Source: National Crime Records Bureau and the Department of Justice via data.gov.in.

title: Air Quality Explorer — what India's monitoring stations are reading, and where there are none
description: Station-level readings from India's Central Pollution Control Board network: 502 continuous monitors across 265 cities in 30 states, for PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2, ozone, carbon monoxide and ammonia. Also maps the network itself — stations per 10 million people by state, from Delhi's 26.8 to Jharkhand's 0.6, and the six states and union territories with no station at all. A state with no station is not a state with clean air; it is a state with no measurement. Source: CPCB via data.gov.in.

title: Case Outcomes Explorer — what happens after a crime is registered in India
description: NCRB Crime in India 2023, state by state, on outcomes rather than counts: chargesheeting rate, conviction rate and how much is still pending, for IPC crime, crime against women, atrocities against Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, cyber crime and crime against senior citizens. Atrocities against Scheduled Castes reach a chargesheet more often than IPC crime overall (81.2% against 72.7%) and convict far less often (31.9% against 54.0%) — the gap opens in court, not at the police station. Deliberately does not rank states by crime, because registered crime measures reporting as much as it measures crime.

title: MGNREGA Explorer — how much of the hundred days actually arrives
description: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act owes every rural household 100 days of paid work a year on demand. District by district from 2018-19: days actually provided (42.7 on average in 2025-26), the 4.0% of working households that reached the full hundred, women's share of person-days against the Act's one-third floor, and average wage per day. 757 districts, searchable by name. Source: Ministry of Rural Development via data.gov.in.

title: The Results Chain
description: The results chain, made clickable. Six large Indian programmes drawn as the same five links — MGNREGA, Swachh Bharat, the Right to Education, ICDS and Poshan, Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY and PM-KISAN — with each link marked by how it is actually measured: a public system updated daily, a national survey every few years, an independent study, or nothing. The counting stops between outputs and outcomes in all six, which is exactly where attribution begins.

title: Resources, Agency, Achievements
description: Naila Kabeer's framework for measuring women's empowerment, made clickable. Four Indian series from the NFHS and the PLFS, each drawn beside the companion series from the same instrument that changes how it reads: lifetime spousal violence against the last twelve months, labour force participation against its U-shaped education curve, household decision-making against who justifies wife-beating.

title: Theories of Development
description: 12 theories of how development is supposed to work, each drawn as a causal chain you can step through, placed on four axes built for South Asian material, and set against what the evidence shows. Global canon and Indian traditions in one filterable catalogue.

title: Village swaraj and the economy of permanence
description: An economy should be organised around the village as a largely self-sufficient unit producing for local need with local labour, because centralised industrial production concentrates power, displaces the labour of a country that has labour to spare, and cannot be sustained by everyone. M. K. Gandhi J. C. Kumarappa, 1909–1948. The causal chain drawn step by step, four placements with the reason for each, and what the evidence says about the claims.

title: Annihilation of caste and state socialism
description: Caste is a division of labourers rather than of labour, held in place by endogamy and by religious sanction, and no economic programme that leaves it standing will reach the people at the bottom of it. B. R. Ambedkar, 1916–1956. The causal chain drawn step by step, four placements with the reason for each, and what the evidence says about the claims.

title: Dependency and unequal exchange
description: Poor countries are not behind rich ones on the same road; they are poor because of the way they are joined to rich ones, and the terms of that connection get worse over time. Raúl Prebisch Hans Singer Andre Gunder Frank Samir Amin, 1950–1970s. The causal chain drawn step by step, four placements with the reason for each, and what the evidence says about the claims.

title: Development with unlimited supplies of labour
description: A poor country holds a reserve of labour whose withdrawal from farming costs almost no output, so a modern sector can expand for decades at a flat wage, and everything the expansion earns above that wage is available to reinvest. W. Arthur Lewis, 1954. The causal chain drawn step by step, four placements with the reason for each, and what the evidence says about the claims.

title: Planning for the capital goods sector
description: In an economy that cannot count on importing machines, the long-run growth rate is set by how much of today's investment goes into making machines rather than consumer goods, so the plan should hold consumption down and build heavy industry first. P. C. Mahalanobis Jawaharlal Nehru, 1953–1961. The causal chain drawn step by step, four placements with the reason for each, and what the evidence says about the claims.

title: The stages of economic growth
description: Every society passes through the same five stages on the way to a modern economy, and the one that matters is a short take-off in which investment roughly doubles as a share of national income. W. W. Rostow, 1960. The causal chain drawn step by step, four placements with the reason for each, and what the evidence says about the claims.

title: The environmentalism of the poor
description: Environmental conflict in a poor country is a distributional fight over who may use a resource that people live on, not a contest between growth and nature, and the people defending the resource are usually its poorest users. Chandi Prasad Bhatt Sunderlal Bahuguna Gaura Devi Ramachandra Guha Vandana Shiva, 1973–present. The causal chain drawn step by step, four placements with the reason for each, and what the evidence says about the claims.

title: Capabilities and human development
description: Development should be measured by what people are actually able to do and to be, because income and even goods say nothing about what a particular person can convert them into. Amartya Sen Mahbub ul Haq Martha Nussbaum, 1979–present. The causal chain drawn step by step, four placements with the reason for each, and what the evidence says about the claims.

title: The dominant proprietary classes
description: India's industrial stagnation was not a planning error but the predictable output of a state serving three propertied groups, none strong enough to rule and all strong enough to be paid off, so public money went into subsidies rather than investment. Pranab Bardhan, 1984. The causal chain drawn step by step, four placements with the reason for each, and what the evidence says about the claims.

title: Stabilise, liberalise, privatise
description: Poor countries are poor because prices are distorted by their own governments, so the sequence is to close the fiscal gap, let prices find their level, open to trade and investment, and get the state out of production. John Williamson, 1980–2000. The causal chain drawn step by step, four placements with the reason for each, and what the evidence says about the claims.

title: Institutions as the fundamental cause
description: Differences in income between countries are caused by differences in the rules governing property, entry and power, and those rules were largely set long ago by whether a place was settled or extracted from. Douglass North Daron Acemoglu Simon Johnson James Robinson, 1990–present. The causal chain drawn step by step, four placements with the reason for each, and what the evidence says about the claims.

title: Randomised evaluation and the small-question turn
description: Grand theories of development cannot be tested, but specific questions about specific programmes can be, by assigning them at random and comparing, and enough answered small questions is a better guide to policy than any answered large one. Esther Duflo Abhijit Banerjee Michael Kremer, 1997–present. The causal chain drawn step by step, four placements with the reason for each, and what the evidence says about the claims.
